result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_cohesion()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get cohesion (minimum node cut size). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20535-L20579){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_cohesion() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The cohesion is the minimum number of nodes whose removal would disconnect the graph. Also called node connectivity. Only defined for undirected graphs. Returns `0` if already disconnected. Note: Current implementation provides an upper bound (minimum degree) for efficiency. Exact computation requires sophisticated algorithms. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum node cut size. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is directed. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} This 4-cycle has minimum degree 2, so its cohesion (upper bound) is 2: ::: {#79856d7b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") .add_edge("D", "A") ) # Returns 2 graph.get_cohesion() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
